meta.title: Herbalist — clinic management for Chinese medicine
meta.description: Clinic management for Chinese medicine: patients and medical files, calendar and online booking, treatment records, a herb and formula library with photographs, inventory, billing, a patient portal and equipment price comparison.

hero.title: Your clinic, in order
hero.body: Everything a Chinese-medicine clinic needs in one place: patients, the calendar, treatments, herbs, stock and billing. Built for the phone and the desk, with a portal for patients.

screens.title: What it looks like
screens.dashboard: The dashboard: today's appointments, tasks, income and patients at a glance
screens.calendar: The week's diary, with rooms and treatment types in colour
screens.treatment: The treatment page: complaint, diagnosis, points, tongue and pulse, dispensing
screens.patient: The patient file: details, history, appointments, documents and consents
screens.phoneCalendar: On the phone: the day's diary

patients.title: Patients and medical files
patients.body: Medical history, documents, signed consents, and the whole file in one click.

calendar.title: Calendar and online booking
calendar.body: A diary per practitioner and room, reminders, and a page where patients book for themselves.

records.title: Treatment records
records.body: Diagnosis, points, formula and dosage, tongue photographs, and a 3D body for the points.

herbs.title: Herb and formula library
herbs.body: Hundreds of herbs with photographs of the material, classical formulas, and side-by-side comparison.

inventory.title: Inventory and dispensing
inventory.body: Batches, expiry, low-stock thresholds, and automatic deduction on every dispensing.

billing.title: Billing and packages
billing.body: Invoices, payments, treatment packages, and treatment confirmations for health funds.

portal.title: Patient portal
portal.body: Questionnaires before the visit, consents, upcoming appointments and the documents you shared.

prices.title: Equipment price comparison
prices.body: Needles, moxa, cupping and more from several shops, with a link to buy beside every price.

trust.title: Built to keep the data safe
trust.isolation: Each clinic sees only its own data, and the separation is enforced in the database itself.
trust.audit: Every look at a patient file is recorded, and whoever runs the clinic sees who reached what and when.
trust.storage: Data is stored in Europe and encrypted, in transit and at rest.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.subtitle: What is accessible, what is not yet, and who to contact
accessibility.intro: We treat accessibility as part of the craft rather than an addition to it. This system is built so that everyone working in the clinic can use it — with a mouse, with a keyboard alone, or with a screen reader.
accessibility.standard: The system is built to Israeli standard 5568, which follows WCAG 2.1 level AA. This statement is updated as the work continues.

done.keyboard: Full keyboard navigation on every screen — menus, filters, table sorting and the acupuncture point chart included — with a visible focus indicator throughout.
done.contrast: Every colour pair that carries text is measured automatically against the 4.5:1 requirement. The check runs on the built code and fails if a new pair falls below the threshold.
done.landmarks: Semantic HTML: a correct heading hierarchy, navigation, main content and header marked as such, and a skip-to-content link at the top of every page.
done.labels: Every form field has an associated label, and every error message is linked to its field and announced — not signalled by colour alone.
done.rtl: Full right-to-left Hebrew support, including menus, tables and dialogs mirroring correctly, while phone numbers and Latin codes keep their own direction.
done.zoom: The layout is built in relative units and stays usable at 200% text zoom.
done.motion: No flashing animation, nothing that moves on its own, and no time limit on completing a form.
done.automated: Automated checks run on every code change: contrast is measured from the stylesheet across 101 pairs, and axe checks labels, accessible names, heading order and direction.

accessibility.gapsIntro: This list is deliberately specific. A statement that claims full conformance and is wrong is worse than one that names its own limits.

gaps.screenReaderAudit: A full manual pass with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver) has not been done yet. Fixes so far were driven by the code and by automated checks.
gaps.bodyMap: The acupuncture body chart is shown both as a 3D model and as a flat drawing. The 3D model is an image only; every point marked on it also appears as a keyboard-accessible button beneath it, and in the point list beside it.
gaps.calendar: The calendar view has not had a full accessibility pass. Every appointment is also reachable from the patient file.
gaps.pdf: Uploaded documents are shown as they arrive. If a document we receive is not accessible, we cannot make it so after the fact.
gaps.automatedScope: The automated axe check currently covers the public pages only. The screens behind the login need a test environment with synthetic data, which is not yet in place.

accessibility.contactBody: If something stops you using the system, we want to hear about it and will act on it. Accessibility reports are handled as a priority.
accessibility.placeholderWarning: The accessibility coordinator has not been named. Before this system serves patients, a name, email address and phone number must be entered here — a statement with no way to make contact does not meet the standard.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.subtitle: What is collected, why, who sees it, how long it is kept, and your rights

scope.title: What this covers
body: Herbalist is a practice-management system for Chinese medicine clinics: a diary, patient files, treatment records, prescriptions, billing, a patient portal and phone apps. This document explains what information is collected, why, who sees it, how long it is kept and what your rights are.
It applies to clinic staff who use the system, to patients who use the portal, the booking page and the arrival confirmations, and to the phone apps of both.

roles.title: Who is responsible for medical information
body: The clinic treating you is the owner of the database holding your medical file, and is responsible for it under the Protection of Privacy Law and the Patient’s Rights Law. We, the operators of the system, process the information for the clinic and on its instructions, and use it for no other purpose.
Enquiries about your file go to the clinic. Enquiries about the system itself go to us, at the details at the end of this document.

collected.title: What is collected
body: What is entered into the system by the clinic, by its staff or by you:

items: Clinic staff: name, email, phone, title and licence number, the clinic’s details and personal settings.

Patients: identifying and contact details — name, ID number, date of birth, phone, email and address; appointments; treatment records, diagnoses, prescriptions and images (a photograph of the tongue, for instance); documents and questionnaires; consents with a timestamp and version; invoices and payments.
Payments: card numbers never pass through us and are never stored by us. Payment is taken by a licensed payment provider; we keep only the amount, the date and a reference.
Use and security: an access log (who opened which file and when), sign-in events and failed attempts, network address and browser — for security only.
The phone app: the device type and a notification identifier, only if you turn notifications on.

purposes.title: What it is used for

items: Providing the service: the diary, the file, the records, billing and the portal.
Reminders and arrival confirmations, on the channel the clinic chose: SMS, WhatsApp, email or a phone notification.
Security and access monitoring: knowing who accessed what, and spotting unusual use.
Legal duties: keeping medical records and accounting documents.
Improving the system, from aggregate data that identifies nobody.

body: There is no advertising and no sale of information. Marketing messages are sent only with separate consent, which can be withdrawn at any time.

sharing.title: Who has access
body: Your clinic — its staff, according to their role. On our side — only whoever maintains the system, and only when needed. And the subcontractors that run parts of the service for us:

items: Supabase — the database and storage.
Vercel — hosting of the site and the apps.
An email delivery provider — sign-in links, verifications and documents sent to you.
The messaging provider the clinic chose (SMS or WhatsApp) — receives only the number and the message.
Google (Firebase) and Apple — phone notifications; they receive a device identifier and a short message with no medical details.

body: Each provider receives only what its role requires and is contractually bound to protect the information. Some servers are outside Israel.

security.title: How the information is protected

items: Encryption in transit and at rest, and encrypted backups.
Separation between clinics at the database level: one clinic never sees another’s information.
An access log that cannot be altered or deleted.
A second factor for staff, and a limit on sign-in attempts.

body: No system is completely immune. If a security incident concerning your information is discovered, the clinic and we will notify as the law requires.

items: Medical records — at least the period set by the Patient’s Rights Law and its regulations, after treatment ends too, under the clinic’s responsibility.
Invoices and receipts — seven years, under tax law.
A user account — until you ask to delete it.
The access log — as long as the file exists, because it is part of protecting it.

rights.title: Your rights

items: Access and a copy — the clinic produces a complete “patient file” at a click.
Correction of wrong details.
Withdrawal of marketing consent, at any time.
Deletion of the sign-in account — see “Delete account”.
Deletion of information from the file — subject to the clinic’s duty to keep records.
A complaint to the Privacy Protection Authority.

body: Rights are exercised with the clinic, or through us where the system itself is concerned.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
body: The system uses a sign-in cookie only, to recognise you from page to page. Display preferences — colour theme, screen arrangement — are kept in your browser and are not sent to us. There are no advertising cookies, no cross-site tracking and no third-party analytics.

minors.title: Minors
body: The system is for clinics. A minor’s file is opened by the clinic with the consent of the parent or guardian, who is also the one given access to the portal.

changes.title: Changes and contact
body: A material change to this policy is announced at sign-in, and the date at the foot of the page is updated. Questions and requests go to the details at the end of the document.
This policy is subject to the Protection of Privacy Law, 5741-1981, and the Protection of Privacy (Data Security) Regulations.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.subtitle: What the service is, who is responsible for what, and what happens when it ends

service.title: The service
body: Herbalist is practice-management software: a diary, patient files, treatment records, prescriptions, stock, billing and a patient portal — on the web and in phone apps. Using it is acceptance of these terms and of the privacy policy.

notMedical.title: Not medical advice
body: The system is a tool for recording and managing. The reference of herbs, formulas, acupuncture points and doses is supporting material and no substitute for professional judgement. Every clinical decision is the practitioner’s, and their responsibility.

items: An account is personal and cannot be transferred.
The password and the second factor are your responsibility; every action from the account counts as yours.
Inviting team members and their permissions are the clinic owner’s responsibility.

data.title: The clinic’s information
body: Information the clinic enters belongs to the clinic. We process it under the privacy policy only. The clinic is responsible for obtaining its patients’ consent, for registering a database as the law requires, and for complying with the Patient’s Rights Law. The clinic can export its information at any time.

items: Do not enter information about people without the authority to do so.
Do not try to reach another clinic’s information, and do not circumvent the security mechanisms.
Do not overload or disrupt the service.
Do not use the service in a way that breaks the law.

availability.title: Availability and support
body: We work for high availability and back the information up, but do not promise uninterrupted availability. Planned maintenance is announced in advance where possible. It is the clinic’s responsibility to keep a copy of what is essential to it, such as exported patient files and invoices.

payment.title: Payment
body: Pricing, the term of the engagement and its termination are set in a separate service agreement. [To complete: the pricing model]

termination.title: Ending
body: You can stop using the service at any time. Closing a clinic that holds patient files is done in coordination, because the records must be kept by law: the clinic receives its information, and then it is deleted on our side.
We may suspend an account that breaches these terms or endangers the service, with notice — except in an emergency.

liability.title: Liability
body: The service is provided as is. We are responsible for taking reasonable security measures and for keeping to the privacy policy. We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss; for any other loss, liability is limited to the fees paid for the service in the twelve months before the event. Nothing here limits rights that cannot be waived by law.

changes.title: Changes and governing law
body: A material change to these terms is announced in advance; continued use after the date of the change is acceptance. These terms are governed by the law of Israel, and the competent courts of Israel have exclusive jurisdiction.

deleteAccount.title: Delete account
deleteAccount.subtitle: How to delete, what is deleted, what stays and why

items: Clinic staff: in the system, Personal area → “Delete the account” (the last card). Type the clinic’s name to confirm and press the button.
Patients: in the portal, “My account” (at the foot of the page) → “Delete the account”.
Without access to the account: send a request from the registered email address to the address at the end of this page. After verification, the account is deleted within 30 days.
The sign-in details: email, password and second factor. No more signing in.
Phone and picture.
Membership of the clinic, and personal preferences.
Patients: the link between the portal sign-in and the file. Signing in again requires a new invitation from the clinic.

stays.title: What stays, and why
body: Patients: the medical file stays with the clinic. The Patient’s Rights Law requires the clinic to keep medical records, and deleting the portal account does not change that. Requests about the file go to the clinic.

Staff: treatment records, appointments and prescriptions you signed stay with the name, title and licence number — a medical record must say who treated. Invoices are kept under tax law. The access log stays, because it is what protects the files.

owner.title: Clinic owners
body: The only owner of a clinic that holds patient files cannot delete their account at once: the records must stay with someone. Make another team member an owner and then delete, or contact us to close the clinic properly — the clinic receives its information, and then it is deleted on our side.

timing.title: When it happens
body: Deletion from the app is immediate. Encrypted backups are deleted in the normal backup cycle, within 30 days at most.

library.title: Professional library
library.subtitle: Professional questions answered only from the sources loaded into the library. No answer without a source.

chats.title: Conversations
chats.empty: No conversations yet. The first one opens with your first question.
chats.deleteBody: The conversation and every message in it will be deleted for good.
chats.welcomeBody: Professional questions the library's sources can answer: herbs, formulas, points, patterns. A question is sent to an outside answering service, so no names or identifying details of patients.

library.privacyBody: The library answers only from its own sources and never sees a patient file. A question is sent to Voyage AI and Anthropic to be answered, so do not type names, identity numbers, phone numbers or medical details of a particular patient. The log records who asked, when, and which sources were retrieved; the question itself is not stored.
library.notConfigured: The library is not connected yet
library.notConfiguredBody: Whoever runs the service has not connected the search and answering services yet. Until then there is nothing to answer from.
library.empty: No question yet. Start from one of the examples.
library.placeholder: A professional question, for example: what are the indications of Gui Zhi Tang according to the sources?
